question.text: A younger investor typically has LOWER liquidity requirements than an older investor because:

answer.text: Younger investors have longer investment horizons and fewer immediate cash needs
Regulations forbid elderly from illiquid assets

explanation.text: The Logic: Younger people usually have lesser liquidity requirements than older people because of longer investment horizons and fewer immediate cash needs. The Trap: The other options are not the source-supported reason for the liquidity difference. Note: All investors still need liquidity for day-to-day, emergency, and near-term needs.
